claimBoundary: Calculated by WorldsIndex from the values this release selects (a selection, not a measurement) and one stated stellar parameter set. Not a fitted solution, not a self-consistent publication solution and not a completeness-corrected population. Every value names its formula, inputs and their sources.
stellarRule: stellar-inputs.v1: the NASA stellar-host parameter set (stellarhosts) whose reference equals the reference of the selected planet period or radius; otherwise the set stating the most of effective temperature, radius and mass (ties by source record id). A field that set lacks is taken from the next set in the same ranking, then from the Exoplanet.eu row of the object. Distances follow the same chain (sy_dist, then Exoplanet.eu star_distance). Magnitudes (J, K) come only from Exoplanet.eu.
samePublicationRule: Inclination, impact parameter and radius ratio are not selected by the selection rule; when used, they are the row of the same publication as the selected period or radius (the same source record, else a row citing the same bibcode or reference), never a row of another publication.
stalenessRule: Predicted 1-sigma mid-transit uncertainty sqrt(sigma_T0^2 + (n sigma_P)^2) at +1, +6 and +12 months after the release reference time, from the release's one chosen ephemeris per planet. Priority (our rule, not ExoClock's): alert when the +1 month uncertainty exceeds 30 minutes or half the transit duration; high when the +6 month uncertainty does; medium when the +12 month uncertainty does; low otherwise; unranked when the ephemeris states no uncertainty. Rank 1 is the largest +12 month uncertainty.
propagation: asymmetric finite differences: f is re-evaluated with each input at value + upper error and value - lower error; positive and negative changes are added in quadrature separately. Correlations between inputs are ignored. Inputs without a reported error contribute nothing (listed in uncertaintyOmits).

formulas.label: Stellar luminosity
formulas.formula: L/L_sun = (R*/R_sun)^2 (Teff / 5772 K)^4

citation.text: IAU 2015 Resolution B3 (nominal solar effective temperature 5772 K)

formulas.label: Insolation
formulas.formula: S/S_earth = (L/L_sun) / (a/au)^2

citation.text: Inverse-square law with the stellar luminosity above

formulas.label: Equilibrium temperature (zero albedo, full redistribution)
formulas.formula: Teq = Teff sqrt(R* / (2a))

formulas.label: Bulk density
formulas.formula: rho = 5.514 g/cm3 (M/M_earth) / (R/R_earth)^3

citation.text: Mean density of the Earth 5.514 g/cm3 (IAU 2015 nominal radius and mass)

formulas.label: Maximum angular separation
formulas.formula: theta = 1000 (a/au) / (d/pc) mas (semi-major axis; the apastron separation is larger for an eccentric orbit)

formulas.label: Radius estimated from mass (Chen & Kipping 2017)
formulas.formula: R = C M^S, piecewise: Terran M < 2.04 M_earth (C 1.008, S 0.279); Neptunian < 131.6 M_earth (S 0.589); Jovian < 0.08 M_sun (S -0.044); stellar (S 0.881); C continuous

formulas.label: Mass estimated from radius (Chen & Kipping 2017)
formulas.formula: inverse of the Terran and Neptunian branches; not computed above 14.3 R_earth, where the Jovian branch is degenerate

formulas.label: Habitable-zone edges (Kopparapu et al. 2014)
formulas.formula: Seff = S0 + a T + b T^2 + c T^3 + d T^4, T = Teff - 5780 K, d = sqrt((L/L_sun)/Seff); conservative: runaway greenhouse (1 M_earth) to maximum greenhouse; optimistic: recent Venus to early Mars; valid 2600-7200 K

formulas.label: Fraction of the orbit inside the habitable zone
formulas.formula: fraction of orbital time with r = a(1 - e cos E) between the zone edges, 7200 steps in mean anomaly

citation.text: Kepler's equation over one orbit; edges from Kopparapu et al. 2014

formulas.label: Earth Similarity Index (radius and stellar flux)
formulas.formula: ESI = 1 - sqrt(0.5 [((S - 1)/(S + 1))^2 + ((R - 1)/(R + 1))^2]), S and R relative to Earth

citation.text: Schulze-Makuch et al. 2011, Astrobiology 11, 1041 (flux form of the Planetary Habitability Laboratory)

formulas.label: Snow line (minimum-mass solar nebula scaling)
formulas.formula: a_snow = 2.7 au (L/L_sun)^(1/2)

formulas.label: Tidal locking timescale (order-of-magnitude estimate)
formulas.formula: t = omega a^6 I Q / (3 G M*^2 k2 R^5), I = 0.4 M R^2

citation.text: Gladman et al. 1996, Icarus 122, 166, eq. 9 (assumed initial spin, Q and k2 stated in `assumptions`)
Lovis & Fischer 2010, in Exoplanets (Seager ed.), eq. 14

formulas.label: Astrometric signature
formulas.formula: alpha = (M_p / M*) (a/au) / (d/pc) arcsec

formulas.label: Transit depth (geometric)
formulas.formula: delta = (Rp/R*)^2 (no limb darkening)

formulas.label: Transit duration T14
formulas.formula: T14 = (P/pi) asin[(R*/a) sqrt((1 + k)^2 - b^2) / sin i] (circular orbits; eccentric orbits need the argument of periastron)

formulas.label: Geometric transit probability
formulas.formula: p = ((R* + Rp)/a) / (1 - e^2) (averaged over the argument of periastron)

formulas.label: Hill radius
formulas.formula: r_H = a (1 - e) (M_p / (3 M*))^(1/3) (at periastron)

formulas.label: Roche limit (fluid planet)
formulas.formula: a_R = 2.44 R* (rho* / rho_p)^(1/3); a / a_R is given beside it

formulas.label: Size or mass class
formulas.formula: by radius (Borucki et al. 2011): Earth-size < 1.25, super-Earth 1.25-2, Neptune-size 2-6, Jupiter-size 6-15, very large 15-22.4 R_earth; without a radius, by mass (Chen & Kipping 2017): Terran < 2.04, Neptunian < 131.6, Jovian < 26,600 M_earth

citation.text: Borucki et al. 2011, ApJ 736, 19; Chen & Kipping 2017, ApJ 834, 17

formulas.label: Transmission spectroscopy metric (TSM)
formulas.formula: TSM = s Rp^3 Teq / (Mp R*^2) 10^(-mJ/5); s = 0.190 (Rp < 1.5), 1.26 (1.5-2.75), 1.28 (2.75-4), 1.15 (4-10 R_earth); mass from Chen & Kipping 2017 when none is selected, as in the paper

citation.text: Kempton et al. 2018, PASP 130, 114401, eq. 1 and Table 1

formulas.label: Quadratic limb-darkening coefficients (gray Eddington atmosphere)
formulas.formula: I(mu) = B_lambda(T(tau = mu)), T^4 = (3/4) Teff^4 (tau + 2/3); quadratic law fitted by least squares on 101 mu points at each band's effective wavelength

citation.text: Eddington approximation of a gray atmosphere (Mihalas 1978, Stellar Atmospheres, ch. 3); quadratic law of Kopal 1950
